newsitem.title: FRANCE: Expanded Marseille airport facilties for June 97.
newsitem.headline: Expanded Marseille airport facilties for June 97.

text.p: Marseille-Provence airport said a 32 million franc project to build 15,000 square metres of aircraft aprons should be completed by June 1997.
The decision to expand apron space follows French express and road distribution firm Jet Services launching operations from Marseille in August 1994, an airport authority official said.
In the first 10 months of 1996, Jet Services handled 8,340 tonnes of freight at Marseille, a 20.5 percent rise on the same period last year.
This makes the company the biggest generator of cargo traffic at the airport ahead of L'Aeropostale, Air France Europe and Air Afrique," the official added.
Jet Services operates scheduled overnight airfreight services between Paris/CDG and Marseille using cargo-configurated BAe 146 aircraft.
The additional apron space will be able to accomodate three quieter Category 3 aircraft, Airbus 320, Boeing 727 and BAe146 simultaneously, he said.
Construction work on the new aprons began in October. -Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
